title: Byte Buddies Coding Club
intro: Text 1 is a webpage for a free weekend coding club for primary school children.

visual.text: Your child already loves games. Let them build one.
Free weekend coding for Primary 3 to 6, taught by teenagers who remember being beginners.
A girl of about ten points excitedly at a laptop screen, where a cartoon cat she has made is jumping. Beside her, a teenage tutor sits back with his hands off the keyboard, smiling.

Byte Buddies is run by secondary school students who learnt to code the hard way: by getting stuck, a lot. That is why our tutors never take over the mouse. They ask questions, give hints and wait. Over eight Saturdays, your child will plan, build and share a simple game of their own — and learn that a mistake is just a puzzle to solve.

visual.title: What parents ask us
items: Does my child need a laptop? No. We lend one.
Is it safe? A teacher-adviser is in the room at every session.

visual.text: “Kai used to give up the moment something went wrong. Last week he spent forty minutes fixing one bug and came home proud.” — Mdm Lim, parent of a Primary 4 pupil
Saturdays, 10 am · Bishan Community Centre · next round begins 10 January
Register your child — 20 places per round

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from an interview in a community centre newsletter with Jun Hao, a Secondary 3 student who tutors at the club.
paragraphs: Newsletter: What is the hardest part of tutoring? Jun Hao: Keeping my hands to myself! When a child is stuck, every part of me wants to grab the mouse and fix it in two seconds. But if I do that, the game becomes mine, not theirs. So I sit on my hands, sometimes really, and ask, “What did you want the cat to do? What is it doing instead?”

Newsletter: Do the children ever give up? Jun Hao: Some want to, at first. One boy cried in week two because his character kept falling through the floor. I told him I had once spent a whole evening on the same problem. By week six he was helping the girl next to him. That is the moment I wait for every round.

questions.text: Look at Text 1. What is the webpage mainly trying to persuade parents to do?

options.label: C

scheme.answer: Sign their child up for a free coding club run by patient teenage tutors.

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support what the body text says about the tutors?

scheme.answer: The tutor sits back with his hands off the keyboard while the girl shows the game she made, which supports the claim that the tutors never take over and let the children do the work themselves.
accept: The girl is excited about her own jumping cat and the tutor is not touching the laptop, so it shows the tutors only guide and do not take over the mouse.
